recipe.title: Kipper pâté with orange on toast
recipe.intro: Spanish oranges are at their sweetest and juiciest in February, and their sharpness is just right against smoky kippers in this quick pâté for hungry afternoons.
steps: Put the kippers in a heatproof bowl and pour over enough boiling water from the kettle to cover. Leave for 5 minutes, until the flesh flakes easily. Drain and let them cool for a minute.
Peel off the skin and pull the flesh into a mixing bowl, feeling with your fingers for any fine bones and picking them out.
Finely grate the zest of one orange into the bowl, then cut it in half and squeeze in the juice of one half.
Add the crème fraîche, horseradish and pepper. Mash with a fork to a rough, spreadable paste. Taste and add a squeeze more juice if you like it sharper. Kippers are salty, so no salt is needed.
Cut the peel and white pith off the second orange with a knife, then slice it into thin rounds. Toast the bread.
Spread the pâté thickly on the hot toast, lay the orange slices on top and finish with a little more pepper.
recipe.tip: Covered in the fridge, the pâté keeps for 3 days, and smoked mackerel works just as well in place of kippers.
